From Hiroshima station, reachable by bullet train from Kyoto or Osaka.

tour.overview:
At 8:15 on 6 August 1945, the first atomic bomb used in war exploded above Hiroshima, destroying most of the city and killing some 140,000 people by the end of that year. The city rebuilt itself as a city of peace, keeping the ruined dome of the Industrial Promotion Hall as a memorial. The Atomic Bomb Dome has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1996. An hour away, on the island of Miyajima, the Itsukushima Shrine, built over the water in its present form in the 12th century, is another World Heritage Site and one of the three most celebrated views of Japan.

This private day combines both with a licensed guide. In the morning you visit the Peace Memorial Park and Museum with time for reflection; after a lunch of okonomiyaki, you take the ferry to Miyajima to see the great torii gate, the shrine on its stilts and the island's old streets.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: Hiroshima station or your hotel in Hiroshima
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver, ferry
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; about 6 km on flat ground

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Atomic Bomb Dome.
• The Peace Memorial Park, the Cenotaph and the Children's Peace Monument.
• The Peace Memorial Museum.
• Miyajima: the great torii, Itsukushima Shrine, Senjokaku and Omotesando street.

WHY THIS WORKS
The car and the guide link the station, the park and the ferry pier efficiently, so a day trip by bullet train from Kyoto or Osaka is comfortable.

WHO IT SUITS
Anyone who wants to understand one of the defining events of the 20th century, and travellers with a Japan Rail Pass.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer a lighter day, choose Nara or Kyoto; the museum is moving and some images are hard to see.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The bullet train takes about 1 hour 40 minutes from Kyoto and 1 hour 20 minutes from Osaka; we can book seats. Whether the torii appears to float depends on the tide; at low tide you can walk to its base.

days.name: The Atomic Bomb Dome, the Peace Memorial Park and Museum, okonomiyaki lunch, and Miyajima's Itsukushima Shrine
days.description:
What to expect: Hiroshima's memorials and the sacred island of Miyajima, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets, ferry and lunch.

Your guide meets you at Hiroshima station, at the bullet-train gate, at about 9:00, or at your hotel. A short drive brings you to the Atomic Bomb Dome on the bank of the Motoyasu river. Designed by the Czech architect Jan Letzel and opened in 1915, the building stood almost directly below the explosion; because the blast came from above, its walls and the steel frame of its dome remained standing. You walk into the Peace Memorial Park, laid out by the architect Kenzo Tange on the site of what was the busiest district of the city, past the Children's Peace Monument, decorated with thousands of paper cranes in memory of Sadako Sasaki, a girl who folded cranes hoping to recover from leukaemia caused by the radiation, to the saddle-shaped Cenotaph, which frames the Peace Flame and the dome.

In the Peace Memorial Museum you see what the city was like before and after the bombing, the belongings of victims, and testimonies of the hibakusha, the survivors. Your guide gives context and leaves you time and quiet to reflect. Lunch is okonomiyaki, Hiroshima's savoury pancake layered with cabbage, noodles and egg, cooked in front of you on a griddle.

In the afternoon you drive to Miyajimaguchi and take the ten-minute ferry to Miyajima, an island so sacred that for centuries no births or deaths were allowed on it. Tame deer greet you on the waterfront. Itsukushima Shrine, built on piers over a tidal cove and rebuilt in its present form by the warlord Taira no Kiyomori in 1168, seems to float at high tide, as does its great vermilion torii, 16 metres tall and standing under its own weight in the sea. You also see Senjokaku, a vast unfinished hall ordered by Toyotomi Hideyoshi, the five-storey pagoda, and walk down Omotesando street to taste momiji manju, maple-leaf cakes. You are back at Hiroshima station at about 17:00, in time for a bullet train back.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Meeting at Hiroshima station.
09:15 – Atomic Bomb Dome and the Peace Memorial Park.
10:15 – Peace Memorial Museum (about 1 hour 30 minutes).
12:00 – Okonomiyaki lunch.
13:15 – Drive and ferry to Miyajima.
14:00 – Itsukushima Shrine, the torii, Senjokaku and Omotesando.
16:15 – Ferry and drive back.
17:00 – Hiroshima station.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Tell us your bullet-train times; we can book seats for you.
• The Mount Misen ropeway on Miyajima can be added for a longer day or an overnight stay.
• The museum contains images that may upset young children.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, museum and shrine tickets, ferry and visitor tax, lunch, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: bullet train, Mount Misen ropeway, drinks with lunch.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can we do this as a day trip from Kyoto or Osaka?
faq.answer: Yes, by bullet train: about 1 hour 40 minutes from Kyoto and 1 hour 20 minutes from Osaka. We meet you at Hiroshima station.

faq.question: Is the bullet train included?
faq.answer: No, as many travellers have a Japan Rail Pass. We can book the tickets and seats for you at cost.

faq.question: Are the tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the Peace Memorial Museum, the ferry to Miyajima, the Miyajima visitor tax and Itsukushima Shrine.

faq.question: Will the torii be in the water?
faq.answer: It depends on the tide. At high tide it stands in the sea; at low tide you can walk out to its base. Both are beautiful; we check the tide tables when planning.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, okonomiyaki, cooked in front of you. Vegetarian versions are available.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: The park and Miyajima are wonderful for children; parts of the museum contain disturbing images. Your guide can adapt the visit.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Yes, largely. The park, the museum and the ferry are accessible, and Miyajima's main streets are flat.

faq.question: Can we stay overnight on Miyajima?
faq.answer: Yes, and it is magical: once the day visitors leave, the island is calm and the torii is lit at night. We can book a ryokan.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not customary in Japan, and no one will expect it.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes and respectful clothing for the memorials and the shrine.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. Spring and autumn are mild; on 6 August the city holds its Peace Memorial Ceremony and lantern floating, moving but very crowded.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
